doc-title: AI Skill Trees at ETUCE | AI Skill Trees
meta-description: A maths skill tree from each ETUCE member country, in the language of its own curriculum. Made for the ETUCE conference Balancing AI in Education, Lisbon, 25 November 2026.
eyebrow: ETUCE · Balancing AI in Education · Lisbon, 25 November 2026
heading: Try a skill tree from your own country
lede: Click your country. Each tree maps the national maths curriculum for lower secondary school into the facts, concepts and skills a student needs, in the language of the curriculum.
map-label: Map of the ETUCE member countries. Choose a country to see its tree.
status-building: A tree for this country is being made right now.
status-planned: A tree for this country is planned.
status-missing-curriculum: We have not been able to get the official curriculum yet. Do you know where to find it? Please write to us.
status-later: Coming later: the trees need a right-to-left layout first.
count-ready: {n} countries have a tree so far.
step1-body: Tap any box in the tree. You see what it means, and what it builds on.
step2-body: The page writes an instruction for that goal, from the teacher's text and the shared teaching method. No AI is involved in writing it.
step3-title: Paste it into any AI chat
step3-body: ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, or whatever your school already has. The AI then practises that one goal with you, in your language.
drafts: These trees are first drafts. An AI broke each national curriculum down with our open decomposition prompt, and no teacher in your country has checked them yet. That is the point of the method: a teacher reads the tree, fixes what is wrong, and shares it with colleagues.
translated: This website is translated by AI as well. A method like this should not stop at a language border.
